summary:
A pair of Chinese firms installed Nvidia Corp.’s powerful Blackwell semiconductors in a Shanghai data center linked to Alice Huang, the woman at the heart of a controversy surrounding the US chipmaker. 
The gear installed at the Yangtze River Delta Project included a GB300 NVL72 rack, among Nvidia’s most powerful products, according to a serial number specified in documents submitted to Chinese regulators in November. Shanghai Shuoyao offered the hardware as collateral to obtain a 96 million yuan ($14 million) loan from Shanghai Innovation Bank, according to filings from the lender that were reviewed by Bloomberg News.

title: Isabella Weber's Vision for an Affordability Agenda
title_cn: Isabella Weber's Vision for an Affordability Agenda
summary: The most important word in politics right now is affordability. It was a winning issue in the midterms for Democrats, and one of the reasons why people across Europe are out in the streets protesting: Food, housing, and energy are getting more expensive by the day. During the height of the pandemic, we talked a lot about inflation with Isabella Weber, and her on what governments can do to make life more affordable has evolved into a book called Anti-Fascist Economics: In Defense of Affordability, Dignity, and Democracy. It is part-history, part-manifesto, and it maps out why things got so expensive and what can be done to get prices down. Today, we speak to Weber about why CPI, in her opinion, is a misleading measure, why fridges got cheaper but groceries got pricier, rebuilding state capacity, strategies for price controls, China's strategic pork reserve, and her new book. (Source: Bloomberg)
